message.content: {"brief_rationale":"The doctor correctly recognized right breast BI-RADS 4B as the priority needing tissue diagnosis, used the workspace/records process, clarified frozen versus final pathology, and repeatedly converted the situation into practical breast-surgery follow-up steps. However, during the peri-procedural phase the advice did not tell the surgical/anesthesia team about chronic hepatitis B/liver function, coagulation background, or anticoagulant status, and red-flag escalation did not cover chest pain, dyspnea, or unilateral leg swelling.
